description: Agriculture water governance soil restoration biodiversity livelihoods and rights reinforce long-term resilience.
Wetlands forests soils floodplains local food infrastructure and community governance strengthen resilience.
Precision agriculture AI sensors controlled environments and water technologies expand unevenly.
Production rises through intensification while soil water biodiversity and farmer viability decline.
Land becomes governed by speculative capital carbon markets or large-scale acquisition.
Drought groundwater depletion urban demand and irrigation pressure intensify conflict and scarcity.
Extreme weather supply disruption price volatility and weak safety nets converge into food insecurity.
Extraction pollution insecure rights and weak governance accelerate degradation and vulnerability.
